w: The day was dedicated to Karyakar Din (volunteers' day).
In the evening assembly programs related to the services of volunteers were presented before Swamishri.

At 10.15 a.m., Swamishri arrived at Khavda, a village 75 km from Bhuj and on the border of India. The BAPS has built a colony of 155 houses called Pramukh Swami Nagar after the earthquake destroyed the village ( For details ). Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha at the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir in Khavda. Leading members of the village honored and appreciated Swamishri during the murti-pratishtha assembly. Shri Harikrishna Maharaj (Thakorji) was honored by the local devotees. The assembly concluded with the dedication of the colony to the people of Khavda.
At 6.50 p.m. Swamishri arrived in Bhuj for the evening satsang assembly.

2005.o: New Delhi: Vijayadashmi, Akshardham Prasad Pravesh
w: At 10.30 am Swami arrived at the main entrance of Akshardham complex to perform the rituals of Prasad Pravesh (entry into the complex). Swamishri performed the ritual ceremony before the main entrance. Ishwarcharan Swami and Kothari Swami were with Swamishri, and the rituals by the entrance doors to the right and left were performed by Mahant Swami and Dr Swami respectively. After the Vedic chantings Swamishri untied the golden thread and entered into the complex after Shri Harikrishna Maharaj (Thakorji). Swamishri travelled the distance to the main monument in a golf cart. The entourage passed by the archways symbolising the ten directions, Bhaktidwar, reception counter, Mayur Dwar, Charanarvind and proceeded towards the main monument.

Thereafter Swamishri ritually performed pujan of the doors and entered inside Akshardham monument. Swamishri and senior sadhus performed pujan of the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Guru Parampara and the deities of Sanatan Dharma. During the rituals several sadhus also performed pujan of Gajendra Peeth and Narayan Peeth. Thereafter Swamishri performed arti and blessed the devotees by showering rice grains. Swamishri then blessed the occasion, “Delhi Akshardham Mahotsav ni jai. Akshardham complex has been accomplished through the efforts and services of everyone. It was Yogiji Maharaj’s dream to have a mandir by the banks of river Yamuna. That dream is being realised today. Here we find the murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan that is supreme and divine and will bless all with profound happiness. Today the doors of God have been opened for countless souls. All those who have offered services with mind, body and soul will be blessed with redemption and happiness in life.”

The theme of the one-day shibir (camp), ‘Satsang – His Wish, Our Life’, provided a learning experience for 800 kishores and kishoris in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The object of assessing and improving each individual’s current level of personal satsang was delivered through a variety of speeches, bhajans, multimedia presentations, skits and personal testimonies. The first session of the shibir opened with a spectacular video, explaining the journey of the human soul. This was elaborated with a speech and a drama that clarified the meaning of satsang, culminating in Viveksagar Swami explaining the glory of satsang. The second session of the day provided an opportunity for kishores and kishoris to understand the key elements of the shibir in small discussion groups. The afternoon session was addressed by Swamishri’s attendant sadhus who narrated memorable incidents of their experiences with Swamishri. Addressing the difficulties of youth, Amrutnandan Swami underlined the message that no achievement is impossible with the association of Swamishri. At 7.10 pm Swamishri was greeted with a spectacular dance to the evening session, before the programme moved to an emotional passage as kishores narrated difficult periods of their life to Swamishri, and the manner in which the compassion of Swamishri had rescued them. A collective prayer, Din kahe to din was sung before Swamishri. In his blessings Swamishri revealed, “One needs both faith (shraddha) and trust (vishvas) in Satsang. Faith means consistent spiritual effort. If one falls into bad company in college then one’s life gets disturbed, but by putting in effort one graduates with a degree. Similarly in Satsang one cannot attain spiritual knowledge instantly. By doing satsang with focused effort one graduates. When one imbibes the words of God and the Sadhu one’s life becomes transformed – one’s speech, moral and social behaviour become pure.”

st.t: BAPS News – National Kishore-Kishori Shibir 2007 – Friday 12 October 2007
w: ‘Satsang – His Wish, Our Life’ provided the learning experience for 800 kishores and kishoris during the National Kishore-Kishori Shibir in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on Friday 12 October 2007. The object of assessing and improving each individual’s current level of personal satsang was delivered through a variety of speeches, bhajans, multimedia presentations, sketches and personal testimonies.

The first session of the Shibir opened with a spectacular video, explaining the journey of the human soul. This was elaborated with a speech and a drama that clarified the meaning of Satsang, culminating in Viveksagar Swami explaining the glory of Satsang. The second session of the day provided an opportunity for kishores and kishoris to understand the key elements of the Shibir in smaller groups with sadhus and sanchalikas, respectively.

The afternoon session was conducted by sevak sadhus who narrated memorable incidents of their experiences with Swamishri. Through the accounts of these sadhus, the audience developed a greater bond with Swamishri.

Addressing the difficulties of youth, Amrutnandan Swami underlined the message that no achievement is impossible with the association of Swamishri. His speech, containing inspiring accounts of fellow devotees, provided renewed inspiration to excel further in Satsang.

Swamishri was greeted with a spectacular dance to the evening session, before the programme moved to an emotional passage as kishores narrated difficult periods of their life to Swamishri, and the manner in which the compassion of Swamishri rescued them. A samuh prarthna (collective prayer), ‘Din Kahe To Din’ was sung to Swamishri as the divine atmosphere was experienced by the entire audience.

In his blessings, Swamishri revealed the path to the happiness of Satsang at all stages and circumstances of life, referring to the commitment and determination one offers to a career or business. Swamishri also encouraged everyone to keep good company. He explained that despite appearing repetitive, Satsang contains the bliss of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and one should continue to remain strong and motivated.

On the previous day Swamishri observed the ongoing construction work of BAPS shikharbaddh mandir in Bhadra. After Swamishri’s morning puja the murti of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was honoured by devotees. In conclusion Swamishri blessed the gathering of devotees. “Gunatitanand Swami, Akshardham incarnate, was born here. He inspired satsang in thousands and thus performed a great service on earth. We can have darshan of such a great person’s birthplace and also see the mandir coming up here before us. Though the village of Bhadra is small the great avatar of Akshardham was born here… You strive with faith at work, business, in farming and studying, similarly, by making effort and having faith in the words of God and his Sadhu one can accomplish everything. To become free of all misery one has to abide by the moral commands and also believe oneself to be atma, akshar or brahman .” In the evening Swamishri went to the holy river Und.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had come to the mandir for darshan and was going up by lift. Below stood Bharadi Bhagat Jasha Jiva Vadher of the village of Lodhva. He had been notorious in the village as a hardened alcoholic. His addiction had enslaved him to such an extent that, for the sake of drink, he had once hung his own son upside down to throw him into a well. He did this out of stubbornness because his wife had refused to give him money for drink. So, to emotionally blackmail his wife, he hung his own son over the well. Whatever money he earned each day driving his chhakdo (a motorcycle rickshaw) he would spend on drink, and he would lie in the middle of the road, and sometimes things got so bad that the villagers had to carry him home by his arms and legs. Once he had even bitten his own tongue.

Such a hardened addict was touched by the magic of Swamishri, and he did not even know when such terrible addictions simply fell away. Today this Ahir devotee is a volunteer of the BAPS satsang mandal of that village. Because of his transformation, many people in the village have also turned to satsang. The miracle is that the women teachers who come from the surrounding villages to teach at this village's school now travel in no one's chhakdo except Jasha Vadher's. This is the power of Swamishri's darshan. After giving Swamishri a brief account of his past life, he asked for blessings.

ds.t: New Year blessings for devotees abroad
w: Today, giving New Year blessings for the devotees from abroad, Mahant Swami Maharaj seemed to be in a transcendent mood. A stream of nectar flowed from his lips like this:

"Today is the New Year. We have God and nothing else, and everything is contained in God. So we cannot give anything (other than) God's blessings. We benefit as much as we digest the blessings, and to digest them, there must be conviction. As much conviction and trust as there is, that much is digested, and accordingly the work is done. Maharaj, Swami and the Satpurush, these three are our straight line understanding.

"We are the atma and not the body. Our greatest work is to spread conviction in Maharaj and Swami. It is for this alone that we are born. We have to do everything else because we have a body, but for us, life itself is that this conviction becomes firm deep within our hearts.

"If this is achieved, not even the slightest desire will remain, everything else will be left behind, and we will go about diving in the ocean of infinite bliss. Gunatitanand Swami said, 'Observe the disciplines, understand the true form of God and recognise the true form of the Sant. Such a person is blessed, blessed, blessed; I am pleased, pleased, pleased with him.' So this is all we have to do."
Mahant Swami Maharaj lay down on his bed. The sadhus said, "Swami! The room temperature right now is 28 or 29 degrees."

Swamishri burst out laughing and, remembering Yogibapa, said, "Once Yogibapa was in Luton. He had the room temperature set to 34. Everyone felt very hot." Saying this, Swamishri burst out laughing. Then he remembered Pramukh Swami Maharaj: "Even at 12 degrees, it suited Bapa!"
At the first opportunity, Swamishri remembered both gurus.
